## Why

v8's Waiting rule says a spawn may run in the background and the orchestrator ends its turn with `waiting on: ROLE AGENT-ID`. On Claude Code this woke the outer session with no content on S99 (2026-10-25), and again on all three relays of 2026-10-26 (ork S110, S116, S118), each handing back "waiting on: implementer" minutes after it started. The owner sees these as pings. The retrospective asked for one report per slice (R8.4). The harness offers foreground subagents, and a foreground spawn removes the interim hand-back entirely.

## Failing tests

## Implement

Where the harness can run a role in the foreground, the orchestrator does so and waits. A headless role on another harness is waited on with a foreground wait on its process. An interim hand-back is sent only for an owner question, a permission denial or a failure; `waiting on:` stays as the fallback for a harness that can only spawn in the background.
